claims.text: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 exhibits a ductile-brittle-ductile transition when aged between 550 and 750°C, with the brittle state near 600°C and recovered ductility near 750°C.
The transition is driven by non-monotonic changes in APBE and SISFE within the FCC matrix.
Stoichiometric Ni3Al-like L12 domains form within the FCC matrix during aging.
Aging near 600°C maximizes chemical ordering in the FCC matrix and brings the ordered domains toward Ni3Al stoichiometry.
Strong L12 ordering increases the anti-phase boundary energy.
High APBE restricts cross-slip and forces dislocations into planar slip bands.
Aging produces jagged or serrated B2/FCC phase boundaries concurrently with L12 ordering.
Jagged B2/FCC interfaces concentrate stress where planar slip bands impinge on them.
The localized stresses generated by planar slip at jagged interfaces exceed the material's fracture toughness and cause brittle failure.
At approximately 750°C, the long-range order parameter, APBE, and SISFE decrease.
The reduction in ordering and APBE at 750°C restores cross-slip and ductile deformation.
Ductile transition zones form along phase boundaries at the higher aging temperature.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy consists of a ductile FCC matrix and a B2 phase.
The as-cast alloy has high elongation and lacks significant chemical ordering and jagged interfaces.
Annealing temperature can cause phase evolution or decomposition in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni HEAs.
The brittle regime occurs when the L12 order parameter exceeds a critical threshold associated with near-stoichiometric Ni3Al chemistry while the B2/FCC interface remains jagged.
Ductility is restored if the interface becomes smooth or the order parameter falls below the critical threshold.
The brittle condition should show planar slip traces terminating at jagged B2/FCC boundaries, whereas the ductile condition should show more wavy slip or cross-slip.
APBE and SISFE can be inferred from dislocation dissociation widths and cross-slip frequency in TEM.
An absence of local nanoindentation-property differences between the ordered matrix and interface would indicate that simple phase decomposition is the dominant mechanism.
